messages:
tess: FYI — received a high-priority customer escalation about repeated 504s hitting hosted inference during a traffic spike. customer says errors start ~30s after burst begins and last ~2-3m. they pasted gateway logs. i can reproduce a couple 504s locally w/ a quick burst test. escalating to oncall.
shawn: oncall here. can you paste the gateway error snippets and the request pattern? is it single long requests or lots of short ones?
tess: lots of short concurrent requests, ~120 qps for ~45s. gateway shows: `upstream response timeout` and `504 from inference-gateway` plus a backlog queue growth. customer also reported auth 401 briefly but that seemed transient. logs: ```[gateway] 2026-03-14T15:03:12Z ERROR upstream timeout id=abc123 queued=0 target=pod-xx init_wait=· 504```
maria: initial read — sounds like scale-up lag. we've seen this pattern when model init + cold KV cache takes > readinessProbe timeout so pods are counted not-ready, but traffic still routed to gateway leading to queue backlog and upstream timeouts. also KEDA/HPA interplay can cause delayed scaling if pollInterval + cooldown are too large.
lee: can you `kubectl get hpa` + `keda scaledobjects` for the inference pool? also what's the current `minReplicas` for that pool? if min=0, coldstarts will add latency.
tess: pulling now. `kubectl get hpa -n redwood-inference backend-inference-hpa` -> `DESIRED 1  CURRENT 1  MIN 0 MAX 20`. KEDA ScaledObject shows `pollingInterval: 30s`, `cooldownPeriod: 300s`.
nate: aha — pollInterval 30s + cooldown 300s is aggressive for bursty workloads. with 120 qps burst we'll hit threshold but scaling only sampled every 30s and then HPA takes another window to add pods. model init time for this model ~18s and readiness probe grace 10s. net effect = 40-60s lag.
shawn: immediate mitigation options: 1) bump minReplicas to 2 for that pool (manual scale) 2) reduce KEDA pollingInterval to 5s temporarily 3) route traffic to smaller cached model variant (if applicable) 4) add a short L7 reject with 429 to shed sudden load instead of queuing to gateway. which is easiest now?
lee: I can bump minReplicas to 2 in the cluster (quick), but that's a config change — need approval for cost. for emergency we can do it and tag infra-cost.
tess: customer authorized temporary mitigation. please proceed. also sending them a short note: "we're scaling up now, will follow up with root cause and permanent fix" :thumbsup:.
maria: operational follow-ups (post-incident): - evaluate lowering KEDA poll interval for inference pools serving unpredictable bursts - set reasonable minReplicas for model families with long init times - add readiness probe grace aligned with model init (e.g., readiness.initialDelaySeconds >= model_init_time) - consider prefix/KV pre-warm on reserve nodes for top customers - add canary traffic policy to divert heavy bursts to cached variants - implement metrics alert for queue length growth at gateway to catch earlier
shawn: i'm executing the temporary step now: `kubectl scale --replicas=2 deployment/backend-inference -n redwood-inference` -> scaling triggered. watch logs for successful ready events.
devops-bot: deployment/backend-inference scaled to 2 replicas. (reaction :rocket:)
nate: i'm also submitting a short PR to reduce KEDA pollingInterval from 30 -> 10s for the pool and add a helm value flag so we can tune per-customer. PR link: (will add after merge). test plan: run a synthetic burst test (120 qps for 60s) and collect gateway queue length + pod readiness timings.
tess: repro steps for eng to validate: 1) run locust/vegeta with 120 qps ramp for 60s against staging inference endpoint 2) ensure minReplicas=0 in one pass and minReplicas=2 in another to compare error rates 3) capture `kubectl describe hpa`, keda metrics, and pod logs for model init 4) record time from first overflow to new pod ready 5) check gateway queue length metric (redwood.gateway.queue_length) and set alert at >50 for 30s
maria: long-term fix suggestion: enable proactive warm pools for models with init_time > 10s, or allow a fast-path ephemeral worker that can return a graceful 429 with retry-after header instead of letting gateway queue. also add model-level metadata for init_time so autoscaler can consider it when making decisions.
lee: filing incident ticket in JIRA -> INF-4921, tagging infra and product. assigned to eng-runtime for autoscale policy update and eng-sre for playbook updates.
tess: customer update sent. they reported latency improved after scaling and 504s stopped ~35s after our action. will follow up after root cause & mitigation.
shawn: closing oncall for now but leaving follow-ups open. please add any missing repro data to INF-4921. thanks everyone :heart:
